message: Tell me about the meal you share when you gather.
How do the letters travel between your communities?
What happened when someone failed badly after their baptism?
How did the house-churches decide who could lead?
That makes sense - so was leadership more about reputation than office at this point?
What would an ordinary gathering have sounded like - who spoke, and in what order?
I want to keep exploring this - what did baptism itself actually look like?
This has been really helpful. Thank you, I think I have what I came for.
No, that is all. I am good.
Yes, I would like that.
What was the hardest part of leaving your village for the desert?
I can't stop thinking about what you just told me - it's unsettled something in me I didn't expect. I don't think I can just go back to normal after hearing that.
What does the cell mean to you - why is staying in one place so important?
Is there a word your community uses for the stillness you seek?
How did an elder teach a newcomer - was there anything like a school?
That is really making me think. Did women live this life in the desert too?
What did you eat, and how often?
Did people ever fail and leave? What happened to them?
What is one saying from your elders that you return to most?
How should I carry any of this back into a life full of noise?
How did your school read Scripture differently from a plain literal reading?
I want to keep exploring this - what makes a reading 'allegorical' rather than arbitrary?
Who decided which readings were sound? Was there a rule?
How did a new student begin - what was taught first?
Did your teachers borrow from Greek philosophy deliberately, or was it already in the air?
I'm back - where were we? What role did memorization play for students?
I could keep asking about this all day - how did the school relate to the bishop?
Were there disagreements inside the school itself?
What happened to a student who came to doubt?
What would your school make of someone learning alone, from books, with no teacher?
I'd like to hear from each of you: how did your community decide who could teach?
Chloe, you mentioned households - did that make leadership a family matter?
Papnoute, how would you answer what Chloe just said - does leaving the household contradict her world?
Mar Yausep, what does your community make of both answers?
Did any of your communities let women lead or teach?
Where do your three worlds most sharply disagree?
What did fasting mean in each of your worlds?
Each of you: what was at stake if the community got teaching wrong?
What would each of you say to the others - one thing you'd want them to understand?
Thank you all. What should I sit with from this conversation?
